title: India Drops Physical Boarding Pass Requirement for International Flights From September 1
excerpt: The Bureau of Immigration will stop stamping boarding passes at all international airports, allowing travelers to use e-boarding passes on their smartphones instead.
body:
• India's Bureau of Immigration will stop requiring physical boarding passes at all international airports from September 1, 2026
  • Passengers traveling abroad can use e-boarding passes on their smartphones for immigration clearance
  • Physical boarding passes will still be accepted but will no longer be stamped by immigration authorities
  • A pilot project to eliminate immigration entry and exit stamps for Indian passport holders is also in the works

Passengers flying out of Indian airports will no longer need to carry a physical boarding pass starting September 1, as the Bureau of Immigration has decided to eliminate the stamping of boarding passes at immigration counters across all international airports in the country, officials told PTI on Saturday.

Travelers heading abroad will instead produce an e-boarding pass on their smartphones for immigration clearance. Physical boarding passes will still be accepted at counters but will no longer receive the immigration stamp that was previously required.

Why the Change

The Bureau of Immigration (BOI), which operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs, issued the directive to airport authorities after finding that the physical stamping process was causing "inconvenience" to passengers. Officials cited recurring instances of errors in reading boarding passes due to "improper or incorrect" stamping as an additional reason for the policy shift.

"The matter has been examined by the BOI and it has now been decided to do away with the mandatory requirement of physical boarding passes and the stamping of boarding passes at immigration counters at all international airports in the country."

— Bureau of Immigration officials, quoted by PTI

The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) had already stopped stamping boarding passes for both domestic and international passengers several years ago. Until now, boarding passes were only required for clearance by immigration authorities — a step that is being streamlined effective September 1.

Part of India's Digital Airport Push

The move extends a series of digital upgrades across Indian airports. India's DigiYatra program already uses biometric-based identity verification at airports in Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and other cities, allowing registered passengers to clear checkpoints using facial recognition without presenting physical documents.

In a separate but related reform, India made its digital e-Arrival Card mandatory for all foreign nationals and Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) cardholders from April 1, 2026, replacing the paper disembarkation forms that travelers previously filled out during flights or in immigration queues. That system requires travelers to submit arrival details online within 72 hours before landing.

Officials also disclosed that a pilot project is underway to eliminate the stamping of immigration entry and exit marks for Indian passport holders. Once the pilot is complete, the measure is expected to be deployed across Indian airports, further reducing the time spent at immigration counters.

What NRI Travelers Should Know

For the millions of NRIs and OCI cardholders who fly between India and their countries of residence regularly, the change eliminates one friction point in what has historically been a multi-step airport process. The key details:

  • From September 1, an e-boarding pass on a smartphone is sufficient for immigration clearance at departure
  • Physical boarding passes will still be accepted but will not be stamped
  • Passports remain required for international travel — the change applies only to boarding pass procedures
  • The e-Arrival Card requirement for foreign nationals and OCI cardholders arriving in India remains a separate mandatory process

India joins a growing list of countries moving toward fully digital airport processes. Singapore, Thailand, South Korea, and several European nations have already implemented or are piloting similar paperless systems for immigration clearance.

The September 1 deadline applies to all international airports in India simultaneously. Airlines are expected to update check-in processes to emphasize e-boarding pass availability through their mobile apps. For frequent travelers, the practical advice is straightforward: ensure your airline app is installed, download your e-boarding pass before reaching the airport, and keep your phone charged through immigration.
